variants.name: A-airy-split
variants.direction: THE COMPOSITION: refined split hero, analogous to reference A. Header with wordmark left, navigation right and small outlined Discuss a pilot CTA. Hero around top 45%: left 44% large headline on three clean lines, short supporting paragraph, two CTA buttons; right 50% one elegant prepared brief product panel, very legible. A thin understated mint route around its bottom connects company context, common plan and action. Middle: three outcomes in one horizontal typographic strip separated by light rules, without card boxes. Next lower section a generous two-column section: heading on left, on right a minimal three-step sequence 'Connect the context', 'Coordinate the response', 'Act and learn' with short single-line explanations. Bottom a pale mint audience/CTA band. Overall bright white, navy headline, petrol buttons, mint highlights, spacious premium B2B software landing. The first headline and the product should feel equally important.
variants.prompt:
Create one exquisitely designed desktop LANDING PAGE concept image for AdaptOps, using the two attached images ONLY as approved brand and visual style references. They are pitch slides; transform their language into a real website visitor experience. All visible text must be in English, sharp, clean and correctly spelled. Deliver a flat web page screenshot, approximately 1440 by 1800 portrait 4:5, no browser chrome, no device mockup or photograph, no surrounding artboard. Comparable desktop website with generous 80px outer margins, 12-column grid, professional Inter-like typography, extremely readable hierarchy. Palette white #FFFFFF, navy #061B2B, petrol #075564, mint #63E5BD and pale mint #EFFAF6. Take airy whitespace and bold promise from reference A, coherent product illustration from reference B. Flat precise vector-like UI; subtle borders and restrained shadows only. Small mint angled brand mark next to AdaptOps, consistent across page. No shiny 3D, no hazy decorative glow, no neon, no stock factory photo, no robot, no fake customer logos, no statistics, no testimonials, no pricing. Do not copy the A/B corner labels or slide footer into the website. This is commercial product positioning: no demo, synthetic data, test, benchmark, prototype, implementation status or hackathon words anywhere.
COPY THAT MUST APPEAR, with exact spelling: brand "AdaptOps"; headline "Adapt as fast as your market changes."; supporting copy "An agent that connects market changes to your business, coordinates a response and executes approved actions."; primary CTA "Discuss a pilot", secondary "Explore the approach". Navigation "Product", "How it works", "Who it's for". Three outcomes "Protect customer commitments. Capture new demand. Keep teams aligned.". Audience "Built for operations and procurement leaders in multi-site timber and materials businesses.". Closing "See what your business could do next." with CTA "Discuss a pilot".
The main product visual must show an already prepared company brief titled "Your next response is ready". It visibly connects a market change AND opportunity to company context and a common plan, then human approval and action. Use meaningful concise UI text, never skeleton-loading lines. Compact source chips "Market sources", "Company data", "Past decisions". Product headings "What changed", "What it means for us", "Recommended response". Concise example content: "Supply disruption and new regional demand"; "Protect current deliveries. Qualify additional demand."; "Secure supply. Align stock and delivery plans."; role tabs "Procurement", "Operations", "Sales", "Finance"; strong product button "Review & approve". Include a compact continuation "Approve → Execute → Verify → Remember" which is clear and doesn't pretend a real action has already been completed. The visual is illustrative product UI, no invented real company, no named integration claimed. Keep the full business loop visible without a complex technical diagram.
Below the hero, make a real visitor progression using two distinct concise sections, not generic filler: outcome row with the three supplied outcomes; section headline "One response. Across your business." explaining "Your business context, market signals and past decisions shape one coordinated plan."; audience and closing CTA as final band. Use enough space so it feels refined, readable and calm. Limit secondary paragraph length and avoid dense small labels. This is one complete compact landing page concept, not a slide deck or a moodboard.
THE COMPOSITION: refined split hero, analogous to reference A. Header with wordmark left, navigation right and small outlined Discuss a pilot CTA. Hero around top 45%: left 44% large headline on three clean lines, short supporting paragraph, two CTA buttons; right 50% one elegant prepared brief product panel, very legible. A thin understated mint route around its bottom connects company context, common plan and action. Middle: three outcomes in one horizontal typographic strip separated by light rules, without card boxes. Next lower section a generous two-column section: heading on left, on right a minimal three-step sequence 'Connect the context', 'Coordinate the response', 'Act and learn' with short single-line explanations. Bottom a pale mint audience/CTA band. Overall bright white, navy headline, petrol buttons, mint highlights, spacious premium B2B software landing. The first headline and the product should feel equally important.

variants.name: B-product-canvas
variants.direction: THE COMPOSITION: centered large editorial promise with a panoramic product canvas, analogous to reference B. Header wordmark left, simple navigation and Discuss a pilot right. Centered headline on two lines with maximum 900px width, centered short supporting copy and two CTA buttons. Under it the main large ultra-legible product canvas, about 90% page width, 4 horizontal columns: Company context; What changed / What it means for us; Recommended response with department tabs and Review & approve button; Act and learn with Approve, Execute, Verify, Remember. The first column lists 'Sites & stock', 'Suppliers & customers', 'Commitments & rules', 'Past decisions', not tiny skeletal lines. Product white on extremely pale mint inset, petrol header, thin borders, no heavy shadow. Below canvas a three-column outcome strip with small understated line icons. Lower part an elegant full-width white section 'One response. Across your business.' with the shared-plan sentence, audience and closing call to action. Make the product scene the visual centerpiece. Same fonts, brand, copy, spacing family and portrait output as the other variants, no additional features.

variants.name: C-change-to-action
variants.direction: THE COMPOSITION: an editorial story from market change to coordinated action, still the exact same white/navy/mint brand. Header wordmark and same nav. Hero top 42% split 55/45: very large left-aligned headline with the words 'market changes.' in petrol, subcopy and CTA buttons. On the right an elegant vertical minimal narrative, three linked floating white strips labeled 'A market change', 'An impact on your business', 'A response ready to approve'; tiny source/document icon, company icon, approval icon, restrained mint connective line. No orbit/circular infographic, no duplicate full dashboard here. Beneath hero, place the main prepared company brief full-width as a calm reading workspace, titled 'Your next response is ready', with 3 readable columns 'What changed', 'What it means for us', 'Recommended response', its source chips and department tabs, plus a petrol action strip 'Review & approve' and continuation 'Approve → Execute → Verify → Remember'. This product preview must have enough room and be as legible as A/B. Under it three typographic benefits with thin rules, then audience/closing CTA pale mint band with headline 'One response. Across your business.' and the shared-plan sentence. Editorial flow, extremely airy composition; the larger product panel lower down distinguishes it from the other variants. No extra text beyond the supplied concise copy.
